teaser.text: Rio Tinto is a mining and processing company: it turns ore and minerals into industrial materials that other businesses use. To understand how a dollar moves through it, start with what it sells, then follow the costs, customers and cash.

dividend.title: Rio Tinto dividend
dividend.meta_description: Rio Tinto's dividend per share, cash coverage, future payout drivers and current yield in plain English.
dividend.opening: Rio Tinto's dividend per share was 304.39 GBp in 2025. Its own free cash flow per share was 186.06 GBp, so 2025's post-investment cash generation did not comfortably cover the distribution.
dividend.closing: The full Rio Tinto memo also covers Rio Tinto's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Rio Tinto pay over the years?

paragraphs.text: Iron ore production reached 289,616 thousand tonnes in 2025, up from 276,557 thousand tonnes in 2021. Realised price fell to US$90.0 per tonne in 2025 from US$143.8 in 2021. Rio’s own free cash flow per share fell to 186.06 GBp in 2025, below its 304.39 GBp dividend per share.

blocks.heading: Is Rio Tinto's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: The dividend was US$4.02 per share while calculated free cash flow was US$2.75 per diluted share. Different denominators and payment dates prevent a precise coverage calculation, but the direction is clear: 2025’s post-investment cash generation did not comfortably cover the distribution.

blocks.heading: What could change Rio Tinto's dividend?

paragraphs.text: The latest full-year dividend was US$4.02 per share, while the H1 2026 interim was US$2.11. The base path rises from US$4.90 in 2027 to US$5.20 in 2028 and US$5.50 in 2029, consistent with a broadly stable payout within policy.
